question: What is the biases that the dataset is known to encompass?
keywords: bias biased fairness demographic representation imbalance skewed prejudice limitation
summary: Records the biases that the dataset is known to encompass.
description: A free-form text that describes the different biases that the dataset encompasses.

retrieval.hypothetical_passage: The dataset exhibits biases in its topic distribution and source concentration. Of a random sample of questions, a majority were mathematical in nature, while smaller fractions involved string manipulation, list processing, or other categories. The dataset is sourced predominantly from a single competitive-programming platform or examination corpus for validation and test splits. Models evaluated on this benchmark exhibit lopsided and uneven performance across subjects; they do not perform uniformly, performing notably worse on procedural and calculation-heavy tasks. The topic distribution over-indexes on STEM and certain domains, while non-Western perspectives are under-represented. Gender and demographic imbalance has been documented across biographical text and crowdworker labels.

extraction.instruction: Extract the documented biases of the dataset, including demographic skew, language coverage, sampling bias, label bias, or any other limitation explicitly framed as a bias.
extraction.field_spec: SPDX property `dataset_knownBias`. Free-form xsd:string. Format: short paragraph or semicolon-separated list of named biases (e.g. 'gender skew 3:1 male; English-only; Western-centric topics').
extraction.output_guidance: Look for bias, fairness, demographic-imbalance, or representational-skew discussion anywhere in the context — sections titled 'Bias', 'Biases', 'Discussion of Biases', or 'Bias, Risks, and Limitations' are preferred but not required. Topic-distribution observations (e.g. 'most questions are mathematical', 'predominantly Codeforces'), demographic-imbalance statements, and performance skews across subgroups all count as documented bias. Quote concrete numbers when present. If multiple biases are listed, combine them. Return noAssertion only when no such discussion appears.
